topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and progression
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer frames the lecture by outlining the learning outcomes, the multi-step mutation progression model, and the conceptual framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Deregulated growth signaling pathways in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how mutations in cell-surface receptors and downstream intracellular cascades drive continuous proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Block in terminal cell differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the mechanisms and consequences of differentiation arrest across hematopoietic malignancies and intestinal epithelial tissues.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptotic cell death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how cancer cells circumvent programmed cell death through mutations in p53 and deregulation of mitochondrial apoptosis regulators.

topics.label: Replicative immortalization, senescence, and growth-control summary
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how cancer cells achieve indefinite replication by overcoming telomere shortening and senescence, concluding the review of cell-intrinsic growth-control hallmarks.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming, the Warburg effect, and oncometabolites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss how cancer cells rewire their cellular metabolism toward aerobic glycolysis and how metabolic enzyme mutations drive epigenetic alterations.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the necessity, timing, and molecular balance required for developing tumors to recruit new blood vessel networks.

topics.label: Mechanisms, dissemination, and genomics of metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address how cancer cells disseminate systemically, overcome metastatic inefficiency, and display genomic alterations such as whole genome duplication.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer provides closing reflections on cancer hallmarks literature, practical sessions, and wraps up the lecture.
